name: GHCL Textiles Ltd
title: GHCL Textiles Ltd - 543918 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: GHCL Textiles Q4 FY26 revenue rose 31% YoY to INR375 crore and FY26 EBITDA rose 34% to INR156 crore, with spreads up to INR148/kg from INR123/kg in Q3.
summary.overview: Management described the quarter as strong on both volume and pricing, with demand improving across knitting and weaving and spreads rising from INR123/kg in Q3 to INR148/kg in Q4. Q4 EBITDA was INR52 crore (EBITDA margin about 11.7%) and PAT INR28 crore. Management said Q1 FY27 spreads are likely to hold at Q4 levels, while flagging West Asia conflict, energy prices, inflation and gas availability as risks. The company stated a INR2,000 crore revenue anchor over about three years, targeting FY29-FY30, and a 15-18% EBITDA margin band.

segments.name: Yarn (spinning)
segments.commentary: New 25,000-spindle unit stabilised at optimum utilisation; management estimated spinning revenue of about INR50-60 crore per quarter at full run rate, with Q4 near that level and Q3 about INR35 crore. About 40% of product yarn is sold as yarn, and the rest is intended to be vertically integrated.

segments.name: Fabric (knitted and woven)
segments.commentary: Fabric share of revenue rose to about 12% in FY26 from 8%, mostly on an outsourced model. Target is about 15% of revenue this year; 15 knitting machines are in house and 25 more are due from Q3 FY27.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Exports were about 14% of top line in Q4, up QoQ. Sales are direct to Europe and Bangladesh; US sales go through fabric manufacturers.

guidance_outlook: Q1 FY27 spreads expected to continue at Q4 FY26 levels (INR148/kg); beyond Q1 depends on geopolitics and fuel/gas prices.
FY27 revenue growth guided to continue at about the FY26 rate (about 14-15%), though management said a precise revenue number is hard to give because it depends on prices.
FY26 EBITDA growth expected to continue at a similar level, plus or minus 2%, if geopolitics does not worsen.
Medium term: INR2,000 crore revenue anchor and 15-18% EBITDA margin, with internal target of FY29 to FY30. Management said normal EBITDA for current products is about 15%.

FY27 capex guided at INR100-120 crore, including about INR35 crore for 10 MW ground-mounted solar (commissioning around July-August 2026) and about INR15 crore for knitting machines. Benefit from the 10 MW solar is estimated at INR4.5 crore in FY27 (INR6.5-7 crore full year).
Remaining planned investment of about INR300-350 crore over about 3 years, mainly for fabric and processing. Working capital target of 110-120 days.
Dividend payout retained at 8% (within the 8-12% policy); no buyback planned.
capex_capacity: 25,000-spindle unit commissioned in June 2025, now stabilised; spindles total about 65,000 (40,000 synthetic plus 25,000 new).

Initial batch of knitting machines installed at end of January 2026; a further 25 machines (about 60% expected in Q2-Q3 FY27) take total to 40 knitting machines, about 15-16 tonnes/day, about 12% of volume.
Rooftop solar: 3 MW commissioned in FY26, about INR2 crore incremental benefit; 10 MW ground-mounted solar due for commissioning around July-August 2026.
Land of about 50 acres allotted in PM MITRA Park, Virudhunagar, Tamil Nadu; significant capex to follow, timing and details not yet disclosed.
Of the INR1,000 crore earlier investment plan, about INR675 crore is deployed and about INR300-350 crore remains.
demand_pricing: Cotton prices rose from about INR55,000/candy in December 2025 to about INR62,000/candy currently; domestic cotton availability described as comfortable.
Demand tailwinds in Q4 from US tariff resolution, India-EU FTA enquiries, and Chinese yarn demand (China demand tapering since March 2026, per management).
Domestic demand rose QoQ and YoY; Europe muted for about 1-1.5 years; Bangladesh inquiries strong.
Cotton mix: about 65-70% pure cotton yarn and 35% synthetic blended. Imported cotton about 25-30% of requirement.
Yarn sales: strategic top-brand customers about 40-50% of volume; brand-via-intermediaries about 20-30%; small and medium customers about 20-25%.

qa_highlights.question: Are Q1 FY27 spreads in line with or above Q4 average, and what drives them?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 spreads should continue at Q4 levels, with the upside from demand in export and domestic markets and cotton prices being softer in Q2-Q3 than now.

qa_highlights.question: Gross margin improvement looks small versus spread increase; why?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the gap reflects volume (Q4 volume slightly below Q3, yarn 10,400 vs 10,800 tonnes) and per-kg versus absolute basis. R.S. Jalan said EBITDA rose about 29% QoQ even after excluding one-time income.

qa_highlights.question: Inventory levels and cotton gains?
qa_highlights.answer: About 120 days (around four months) of cotton inventory as on 31 March 2026; purchases to taper. Management said there were no inventory gains in the last year.

qa_highlights.question: Capital allocation: buyback or capex?
qa_highlights.answer: No buyback. Cash to go to the remaining INR300-350 crore investment over about three years and to fabric and processing.

qa_highlights.question: Dividend payout below 10%?
qa_highlights.answer: Raman Chopra said the policy is 8-12% of payout, retained at 8% this year; cash prioritised for growth capex. Dividend about 30% of PAT per management wording.

qa_highlights.question: Path to INR2,000 crore revenue and 15-18% EBITDA margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Anchor is INR2,000 crore; internal target FY29-FY30. Margin driven by product mix, utilisation of 98-99%, and vertical integration; FY27 revenue growth is guided at the FY26 rate with limited room from current assets.

risks_watch: Energy and fuel prices from the US-Iran conflict and West Asia; gas availability risk for the industry; management said GHCL does not use gas in processing.
Downstream price absorption: management said it is unclear whether yarn and fabric buyers will accept higher costs as cotton rises.
Working capital elevated at about 135-140 days due to cotton stockpiling; receivables up about 43% YoY, with payment discipline weakening in Q2-Q3.
Operating cash flow fell sharply YoY (per analyst; company did not dispute).
Rupee depreciation (about 90 to 96/USD cited by an analyst) raises cotton and spares costs even as export realisations rise.
Post-Q1 spread visibility is limited; China yarn demand tapering since March 2026.
Fabric margins are not yet proven: outsourced fabric is volume-led; management said in-house fabric should improve profit.
summary.management_tone: Cautiously optimistic: management was confident on Q1 FY27 spreads and FY27 growth but repeatedly qualified outlook on geopolitics, energy and inflation. Evasive on the exact margin bridge and on FY27 revenue, which it said depends on prices.
key_quotes: As I said before, we are cautiously optimistic.
So whatever spreads we have received in quarter 4, at least it seems to continue in quarter 1.
We are not looking at buyback right now.
I think we have just started our vertical integration journey now.

financial_highlights.change: EBITDA margin about 11.7% (up from about 10%-11% per management)

financial_highlights.value: About INR8-9 crore profit from sale of non-core land parcel
financial_highlights.change: Other income jumped to about INR10 crore

adds.what: 10 MW ground-mounted solar (power, not productive output)

growth.why: FY27 revenue guided to grow about 14-15% (in line with FY26), with Q1 FY27 spreads held at INR148/kg; backing is partial, from the 25,000-spindle unit now stabilised, 25 more knitting machines due Q2-Q3 FY27, and price-driven spreads, with no contracted orders quantified and the INR2,000 crore anchor (FY29-30) left as an aspiration.
